Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion

Record Class LocalizationInputs

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.LocalizationInputs
Record Components:
gyroHeading - gyro heading. Limelight's MegaTag2 needs it.
angularVelocity - robot angular velocity.
chassisSpeeds - chassis speeds, in robot or field frame; only their magnitude is used.
planarAcceleration - in-plane acceleration, in G.
currentPose - the pose the estimator holds right now. The Mahalanobis filter uses it to measure how far a new measurement strays.
public record LocalizationInputs(Supplier<edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d> gyroHeading, Supplier<edu.wpi.first.units.measure.AngularVelocity> angularVelocity, Supplier<edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.ChassisSpeeds> chassisSpeeds, Supplier<edu.wpi.first.math.Vector<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N2>> planarAcceleration, Supplier<edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d> currentPose) extends Record
The robot state that every pose source shares.

It is built once and PoseFusion hands it to every source you register. Sources use it to decide whether this is a good moment to trust a measurement: a robot spinning at 600 degrees per second produces images you cannot do PnP with, and one that has just crashed produces IMU readings that describe nothing.

Every field is optional

A null means "I do not have that datum", and any filter that depends on it is skipped instead of failing. That way you can start with the bare minimum --- a pose and some speeds --- and add sensors without touching the sources.

Acceleration units

planarAcceleration is in G, which is what Pigeon2.getAccelerationX and getAccelerationY return. It is the only field with an implicit unit, so it is worth not guessing it: 

 () -> VecBuilder.fill(
         pigeon.getAccelerationX().getValueAsDouble(),
         pigeon.getAccelerationY().getValueAsDouble())
